summary: The article provides a largely accurate and well-explained overview of the CBDT's new crypto reporting guidance, aligning with OECD standards and existing Indian tax laws for VDAs.

claims.claim: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued guidance aligning India's crypto reporting with global OECD standards.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm CBDT has issued guidance aligning with OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).

claims.claim: It does not introduce new taxes on crypto assets; existing tax laws remain unchanged.
claims.note: The guidance note does not introduce new taxes; existing tax laws (30% tax on gains, 1% TDS) remain unchanged.

claims.claim: The existing tax provisions for Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs) include a 30% tax on gains and 1% TDS on certain transactions.
claims.note: Income from transfer of VDAs is taxed at a flat 30% (plus surcharge and cess), and 1% TDS is applicable on certain transactions.

claims.claim: Under current VDA tax rules, losses from one VDA cannot be set off against gains from another VDA, nor against any other income.
claims.note: Losses from VDAs cannot be set off against any other income, including gains from other VDAs, and cannot be carried forward.

claims.claim: CASPs will file this information annually through Form 167, starting with transactions from calendar year 2026 and the first filings due in 2027.
claims.note: Exchanges will file information annually through Form 167, starting with transactions from calendar year 2026, with first filings due in 2027.

article_title: CBDT's New Crypto Reporting Guidance: What Investors Need to Know
